subject: general
question: In which of the following situations is a liquidity trap said to have occurred?

options.text: Perfectly elastic demand with respect to interest rate
Perfectly inelastic demand with respect to interest rate
Increase in money supply leads to increase in interest rate
Decrease in money supply leads to decrease in interest rate

solution:
The correct answer is __**Perfectly elastic demand with respect to interest rate**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 
 

• A **liquidity trap** occurs when the demand for money becomes **perfectly elastic** with respect to the interest rate. This means that even if the central bank injects more money into the economy, interest rates do not fall further, and people hoard cash instead of investing or spending. 

• In this situation, the **marginal efficiency of capital** is so low that businesses and individuals prefer holding cash to making investments. The economy becomes unresponsive to monetary policy interventions. 

• The concept of a liquidity trap was introduced by the economist **John Maynard Keynes** in the context of his General Theory of Employment, Interest, and Money (1936).
